q: The mass of an object is a measure of the amount of _____ in it.
e: The mass of an object is a measure of the amount of matter in it. Matter here means anything that has mass and occupies space. Weight: the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force.

q: Mass is measured in laboratories using a sliding mass balance or the _____.
e: Mass is measured in laboratories using a sliding mass balance or the Vernier calipers. The physics in this sentence is built around Vernier calipers.

q: The _____ balance is easier to use and also more accurate than sliding mass balance.
e: The electronic balance is easier to use and also more accurate than sliding mass balance. The physics in this sentence is built around electronic.

q: The balance really detects the gravitational pull on the object (weight), but the scale is marked to show the _____.
e: The balance really detects the gravitational pull on the object (weight), but the scale is marked to show the density. Density here means mass per unit volume.

q: The mass of purified drinking water of 1 litre bottle is _____.
e: The mass of purified drinking water of 1 litre bottle is $1\text{ kg}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $1\text{ kg}$.
